chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from some of our companions, from Abū Jamīlah al-Baṣrī, who said:

I was with Yūnus in Baghdad, walking with him in the market, when the seller of al-fuqāʿ opened his beverage, and it spurted out and struck the garment of Yūnus. I saw that he was distressed by that until the sun declined, so I said to him, “O Abā Muḥammad, will you not pray?” He said to me, “I do not wish to pray until I return home and wash this khamr from my garment.”

So I said to him, “Is this an opinion you have adopted, or something that you narrate?” He said, “Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam informed me that he asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about al-fuqāʿ, and he said: ‘Do not drink it, for it is an unknown khamr; and if it reaches your garment, then wash it.’”

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If any of these beverages reaches the body of a person, it renders it impure, and it is obligatory upon him to remove it and purify the place it reached by washing it with water. Once the impurity of these beverages is established by what we have mentioned, then there is no doubt about the obligation of removing them from the place they reach, because it is established that a person is required to pray while there is no impurity on his body or on his garments. Then he, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: The vessels of khamr and all intoxicating beverages are impure; they are not to be used until what is in them is poured out and they are washed seven times with water.

key_terms.أَوَانِي: vessels or containers, which are ruled impure when used for khamr
key_terms.الْأَشْرِبَةِ الْمُسْكِرَةِ: intoxicating beverages, all included in the ruling here
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: a fermented beverage discussed here as legally treated like khamr
key_terms.تَطْهِيرُ: purification of the affected place by washing with water
key_terms.ثَوْبَكَ: your garment, which must be washed if touched by the substance
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: intoxicating wine or liquor, identified here as ritually impure
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it, the direct legal instruction in the narration
key_terms.نَجَاسَةُ: ritual impurity requiring removal before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does al-fuqāʿ make clothes and containers impure in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that al-fuqāʿ is treated as khamr and that if it touches a garment it must be washed. The accompanying legal discussion extends this ruling to the body and to the vessels of intoxicating drinks, emphasizing the obligation of removing najasah before salat (prayer).
